title: gRPC authentication denial preserves method cardinality
status: Focused authorization behavior passes; capability remains prepared
changes: API-key authentication denials now retain the registered unary-unary, unary-stream, stream-unary, or stream-stream method shape and its serializers.
The interceptor resolves the registered handler before deciding how to construct a denial handler; unknown methods remain unimplemented without database lookup.
The enabled loopback test verifies that a missing key on a server-streaming RPC returns UNAUTHENTICATED before acquiring a service database connection.

verification.command: python3 -m pytest tests/test_grpc.py tests/test_grpc_auth_context_lifecycle.py tests/test_grpc_auth_denial_cardinality.py tests/test_grpc_enabled_transport.py tests/test_grpc_error_redaction.py tests/test_grpc_optional_boundary.py -q
verification.ruff: python3 -m ruff check services/grpc/auth.py tests/test_grpc.py tests/test_grpc_auth_denial_cardinality.py tests/test_grpc_enabled_transport.py: passed
verification.compilation: python3 -m compileall -q services/grpc/auth.py tests/test_grpc.py tests/test_grpc_auth_denial_cardinality.py tests/test_grpc_enabled_transport.py: passed
verification.database_or_provider: None used; authentication lookup and service dependencies are mocked. The loopback server binds an ephemeral localhost port and requires host access in this environment.

scope_limits: No TLS, live database/runtime-role, tenant-scope, streaming authorization parity, or REST contract parity was tested.
The optional gRPC service remains private-network only and has no configured TLS credentials in the candidate profile.
